# NOTES: 2 BOOKS

## BOOK 1: The Boy Traders; or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers
Harry Castlemon, Frank Nelson Series. Gutenberg 56868.

**Cast:** Uncle Dick (captain, schooner *Stranger*, old sailor, meerschaum pipe). Frank Nelson (nephew, sailing master). Walter Gaylord (paymaster, keeps safe key). Eugene Gaylord (flute, Henry rifle). Archie Winters (Frank's cousin, impulsive, "Yankee"). Fred Craven, George Le Dell, Featherweight, Perk (Phil Perkins). Dick Lewis and Bob Kelly (trappers; Dick: wild yells, fast). Mr. Baldwin (first mate). Mr. Parker (second mate). Lucas (old boatswain's mate). Barton (coxswain). Rodgers, Freas, Brown, Stevens, Doctor (negro cook), Old Neptune. Bellville = home town. Chase and Wilson stayed in Bellville. Jasper Babcock (Bellville). Mr. Gaylord (father, plantation, "Lost Island").

**Ch I, The Sandwich Islands:** Cyclone quiz with Frank (two motions, rotary and progressive; SH rotation; escape NE). Recap: Tycoon whaler at Honolulu; Captain Barclay wounded; Frank had been shanghaied and became commander. Walter captured by robbers, held at Potter's ranche, rescued by Dick and Bob. Archie lassoed wild horse. Zack and Silas robbed emigrant; box held brass clock-like machine (Pike's quartz mill). Three weeks at Oahu; Father Damon preached; ride around island took 8 days. Hilo: surf-board. Mr. Kanaker, native swimmer, speaks good English. Archie and Eugene dare each other; both back out. Kilauea volcano; trappers stay on veranda, watch the glow, frightened. Boys walk in crater, chunks of lava, cold lava 14 inches. Trappers decide to follow Uncle Dick to Africa.

**Ch II, The Gale:** Mangrove Islands; Frank shells village with 30-pounder "Long Tom." Crowd of natives flees from ambush. Dick: "quid" whale fear. Rodgers: Davy Jones's locker. Schooner runs out to sea. Cabin battened down, trappers locked in. Eugene complains. George cites Tecumseh (sunk by torpedo, Mobile Bay, 112 men). Gale all night. Damage: flying jibboom, topmasts gone, bulwarks smashed; sailor washed.

**Ch III, The Last of Long Tom:** Four weeks of calm, collecting curiosities. Cyclone approaches; Mr. Baldwin explains (calm at centre, 15 minutes, off Mauritius). Consort ship (white hull, black stripe) also turns. Gale three days; schooner dismantled, one jury mast. Drives toward island. Frank pumps. Long Tom thrown overboard by mate and two sailors with axes. Schooner passes breakers, grounds lightly, anchors within rifle shot. Dick fires 20-pounder shrapnel at canoe fleet (~300 natives), four boatloads emptied. Then big ship seen drifting helpless.

**Ch IV, A Change of Programme:** Ship is Sea Gull (from Melbourne/Hobart Town, English). Shrapnel scatters natives on beach. Boats rescue survivors; Archie counts 11. Frank officer of deck, puts Bob and Perk on anchor watch. Uncle Dick: 4 rescued men are escaped convicts (Van Diemen's Land/Tasmania). Refit at Hobart Town planned, then Natal. Giant "Waters" (Englishman, huge). Frank, Archie talk at night. Perk: "Dick can't stand up against an avalanche." Archie: "You'll see."

**Ch V, The Two Champions:** Waters swaggers; Mr. Parker orders him "for'ard." Waters threatens ("hif you knowed me"). Barton reports Waters asked about strong box, crew pay. Waters strikes Lucas; mutiny with handspike, roars "Stand by me, mates." Dick Lewis yells, dodges handspike, tackles giant. Master-at-arms irons Waters; Uncle Dick: 24 hours without food per word. Uncle Dick lectures the three friends at mast. Dick given respect by crew. Archie challenges Dick vs horse race. Decision: go to Natal, not Asia.

**Ch VI, The Consul's "Clark":** Schooner sails from island with 13 guns fired. Three weeks to Hobart Town. Waters sees spire, says "We're back ere after hall our trouble." Convicts under guard. Fowler, consul's clerk, kid gloves, "Aw!" speech, says "ham" "hif." Mr. Baldwin refuses to hand over men without written order from Captain Gaylord. Police arrive; convicts removed. Fowler tells Frank that Waters belongs in chain-gang, escaped four times. Dinner with Englishmen; Club refuses wine. Archie's "Rocky Mountains" proportion joke (Ireland 33,000 sq mi; Rockies 980,000 sq mi). Uncle Dick bribery story: Bendigo mines, gave policeman an ounce of gold (~$17.50).

**Ch VII, More about the Clerk:** Mr. Wilbur sheep station (Uncle Dick's friend). Horse race: Archie master of ceremonies; Eugene rides Wilbur's horse bareback; Dick gets flying start, wins, easy. Melbourne; mines; Archie's horse stolen by bushrangers. Hobart Town: Fowler asks Frank about strong box, Walter, navigation; Frank says he brought Stranger round Horn. Fowler pumps info. Schooner comes up river. Fowler takes Club on wild goose chase; Frank locked in cabin, wakes to find schooner under way. Archie at table with Bob (revolver). Waters and Fowler enter.

**Ch VIII, On the Quarter-deck again:** Waters: "We're working for liberty." Frank made captain, Archie mate. Bob was ticket-of-leave man; Fowler held a post and had consul's contacts. Sea Gull convicts had shipped as sailors. Three crewmen join plot. Seizure: mates tied, gagged, left in bushes; Uncle Dick's crew taken ashore. Fowler sends sailors on horse race lie; Fowler gets Mr. Baldwin off ship. Convicts swim out and seize vessel.

**Ch IX, A Yankee Trick:** Fowler plans to lure Walter down lane; Bob to capture him. Archie joins Walter; Bob seizes Archie by mistake (Panama hat, black suit). Archie taken aboard. Waters & Frank talk. Frank avoids steamer by sailing back at night with lights out. Waters: "That's a regular Yankee trick." Archie gets Frank a loaded revolver; reveals two revolvers under Uncle Dick's mattress. Archie: "I wasn't born" joke.

**Ch X, Archie Proves Himself a Hero:** Archie irons sleeping Waters with Doctor's help. Captures Bob, Fowler, others. Brown, Stevens, Doctor help. Waters obeys Archie. Doctor guards prisoners with musket. British steamer; lieutenant (gray-headed, unnamed) and midshipman Kendall board. Frank refuses to surrender schooner; flag dispute.

**Ch XI, An Obstinate Captain:** Kendall and Archie fight over flag. Frank: "Haul it down yourself." Lieutenant leaves. Club tug arrives with Uncle Dick, Wilbur, trappers. Uncle Dick: Walter nearly... three foremast hands discharged at Hobart Town. Schooner heads to Natal with three new American sailors. Trappers' fear of Africa.

**Ch XII, Buying an Outfit:** Natal. Uncle Dick meets Scotchman McGregor ("Mack"), ex transport-rider, bought English colonel's outfit at Grahamstown: span of six yoke oxen; wagon 18 ft x 4 ft, green-bough cover; a dozen "salted" horses; double-barrel elephant gun (Frank's "giant" rifle, number 3). Lottery by hat: Frank draws #3 (vicious horse, heavy rifle). Archie gets thoroughbred and silver-mounted rifle. Kaffir servants (letter: good cook, thief). Boers, Griquas (enemies, trade). Six weeks trek.

**Ch XIII, A Surly Boer:** Mynheer Schrader (surly field cornet). Refuses trade. Mack says Schrader sent son to warn others. Griqua gun repair: Frank files notch; native named "Jones" (Archie's joke). Schrader angry: Frank armed Griquas. Lion veldt warning; "I dare you to stay there" (Eugene challenges Archie and Fred to spend night at fountain shooting-hole).

**Ch XIV, A Troop of Lions:** Night at fountain. Archie, Fred, Eugene in shooting-hole. Jackal yelping. Archie shoots (double-barrel), Eugene and Fred fire 39 shots. Uncle Dick and Frank come with firebrands.

**Ch XV, "Where's My Horse?":** Targets were wild dogs, not lions (Mack says). Dick: Mack assured no danger from lions. Schrader warns of Bushmen; Kaffirs plan desertion. Uncle Dick's horse neighs; Archie's horse lost in thornbush, returns. Mack seems uneasy about rope. Walter on guard with Bob.

**Ch XVI, Deserted:** Mack takes Walter's horse and gun, tells Walter a Kaffir stole Uncle Dick's double-barrel. Mack deserts. Eugene and Perk discover Kaffirs still there, but Kaffirs leave with oxen and property. Walter drives badly (whip hits own ear). Griqua village; Zulu delegation (150 warriors, elephant tusks) demands rifle; Uncle Dick refuses. Dick's war dance and yells; Zulus flee.

**Ch XVII, Conclusion:** Griquas believe Dick is medicine-man. Griquas gave milk and corn. Griqua guides desert; oxen lead way. Ravine ambush: chief shot by Bob Kelly; Zulu spears kill oxen and horses. Archie's horse killed; Frank saves Archie, spear hits haversack. Trappers' horses killed, they fight on foot. Frank keeps haversack. Griquas return. Boers trade; 80 oxen. Mack sold Uncle Dick's horse and gun at Grahamstown; gone. Homeward: Lost Island; Bellville; cannons salute; Gaylord mansion; old Sam; week's festivities. Epilogue: Frank lawyer (fishing, Rangeley Lakes, possible politics); Archie civil engineer, married; Chase and Wilson orange plantation Florida; Fred Craven revenue service lieutenant; Jasper Babcock cotton factor Bellville; George Le Dell cotton in Memphis (Archie's brother-in-law); Phil Perkins steamers New Orleans–Galveston; Walter and Eugene run plantation; Uncle Dick lives in cabin; Banner and Stranger still afloat.

## BOOK 2: The O'Ruddy: A Romance
Stephen Crane and Robert Barr (1903). Narrated by Tom O'Ruddy ("The O'Ruddy"), first person. Gutenberg 29573.

**Cast:** Tom O'Ruddy (narrator, 18, Glandore, Co. Cork; "chieftain ancestors"; father died; father once "a grand rogue"). Father O'Donovan (priest). Mickey Clancy (steward). Patsy O'Gorman (miser, died, left £300 for pilgrimage to Rome). Lord Strepp / Arthur (son of Earl, later Earl of Westport's heir; handsome, honourable). Colonel Clarence Royale (duellist, middle-aged, gouty). Reginald Forister (dark-skinned, Earl's shipping partner, "little black rascal," duellist, sweetheart Nell, child). Earl of Westport (old, sick, bright eyes, cruel, "Straw! straw!"). Countess of Westport (tall, "old harridan," "baboon"). Lady Mary Strepp (beautiful, sister of Strepp). Paddy (red-headed Irish vagabond; hair a "burning haycock"; "lashings"). Jem Bottles (highwayman, ballads: 7 Bristol, 3 Bath; mother Dame Bottles). Dr. Chord (little scientist, gossip, "Strap me!"). Fullbil (literary master). Bobbs (dramatist). Fancher (critic). Sir Edmund Flixton. Strammers (Westport gardener with blunderbuss). Josiah Brooks (lawyer, Temple, cold). Tom Peel (smuggler, giant, leader of nine men). Lord Strepp captured in tunnel. Sir Goddard Oxenbridge (ghost, sawn in two at bridge).

**Ch I:** Father's will: papers for Lord Strepp (now Earl of Westport), lent breeches in France. Papers worth returning; "you may get the back of his hand." Tom travels to Bristol; inn; supper; Royale and Strepp; Forister's remarks; Tom calls "That, sir, is a lie." Royale challenges. Strepp visits; duel at daybreak. Tom kicks Forister out of inn. Earl and Countess arrive. Earl: "The O'Ruddy? Rubbish!" Tom's glimpse of eyes in hood. Royale and Strepp laughing from railing.

**Ch II:** Tom finds Paddy (red hair, "Irish keening") in rain; dresses Paddy in Tom's old velvet clothes; sword on string. Paddy's "lashings" confusion. Duel: Tom laughs in Royale's face, Royale furious, Tom pricks sword arm; Strepp stops it ("Enough. Back, Colonel!"). Royale: "I couldn't reach him." Crowds of boys. Strepp: "Most remarkable case."

**Ch III:** Papers missing; Paddy had them (one boot worn). Tom accuses Forister. Forister gone to Bath. Tom meets Jem Bottles at oak tree; highwayman, his mother's cottage; Tom borrows horses; Dame Bottles blesses. Tom gives Jem 14 guineas? (Jem and Tom each had 15 guineas total.)

**Ch IV:** Bath: landlord says Forister went back to Bristol. Tom borrows 5 guineas from Jem. Wayside inn near Bristol: Jem's sweetheart chambermaid; Paddy has barricaded a small black man (Forister) in room. Forister taunts Tom: "king of the Irelands." Tom, Paddy, Jem arrive at Bristol inn.

**Ch V:** Forister denies papers; threatens to kill Tom. Tom at Bristol inn; Earl's valet; Strepp and Royale. Earl's chamber: Earl: "Worthless! Straw!" Lady Mary enters, "Father, make me easy!" Earl accuses Tom of ruining him.

**Ch VI:** Papers fall from pillows; Tom gives them to Mary (kneels, sword on floor). Strepp and Royale offer swords; Tom says "men of peace." Royale: Forister "one of finest swordsmen in England." Forister is "my father's partner in shipping trade." Strepp: "Mary is fond of him." Royale and Strepp: mutual apology.

**Ch VII:** Tom's brooding about estate at Glandore; Forister visits Tom's room, threatens about Nell (Bristol girl); Tom mentions "the child"; Forister sheathes sword. Royale enters.

**Ch VIII:** Royale: "Ponsonby and Stewart" duel talk. Strepp and Royale bow ritual at door. Tom in garden: Countess and Mary talk; parrot calls "Pretty lady!"; Countess orders parrot away. Lady Mary speaks to Tom, warns "Don't fight Forister, 'tis certain death." Tom refuses to run. Mary: "Go in your glowing stupidity."

**Ch IX:** Father's stories (mention of Mickey, lancer, walnuts). Royale: Mary's note "God spare you!" (given to Royale). Tom: Royale saw Mary as baby in bath (jealous). Duel: Tom attacks, wins; sword into Forister's left shoulder. Forister carried off on pallet. Tom looks at window hoping to see Mary; empty.

**Ch X:** Tom famous; servants flee. Coffee room: Countess chases Tom around table; ivory fan hits bystander's eye.

**Ch XI:** Forister carried away; Strepp with sword. Lady Mary and Countess went to London. Royale and Strepp at Bath inn. Tom rides to Bath; horse lamed in puddle. Tom finds Paddy and Jem with papers near haycock: they robbed Earl's carriage on Bristol road; Paddy read Mary's letter (Mickey and pig), Jem divided gold. Tom takes papers.

**Ch XII:** Tom plans: go to London; Jem and Paddy to Bath separately. Earl at Bath inn; Tom says "Lady Mary Strepp" is rightful recipient; Earl sees Tom's lineage; "why didn't you read the papers?" Tom: "a tutor."

**Ch XIII:** Earl says he knows of love; offers Mary (flirts). Tom flees chamber. Countess and Paddy fight in hall: Countess drunk; Paddy escapes. Paddy and Tom talk of food, manners.

**Ch XIV:** Countess enters Tom's room; Paddy holds her against wall with chair; Tom slides under bed, escapes. Landlord beaten by Tom. Paddy and Tom to London. Paddy: "Grand ladies... Mag Cooligan." Tom cuffs Paddy.

**Ch XV:** Road to London; Paddy's views on English ("hard heads"), Irish, Father Corrigan; "traducing." Inn: "Mr. O'Ruddy celebrated Irish swordsman" in taproom.

**Ch XVI:** Tom confronts Jem in taproom; "sticadoro proderodo sliceriscum" test; "A blue one." Tom teaches Paddy and Jem to be grand servants (bottles in fists). Jem and Paddy discuss.

**Ch XVII:** London; Paddy's hair cut; sixteen-year-old sneers; shopkeeper directs to "Pig and Turnip" inn, Bishopsgate Street. Innkeeper: Mr. Fullbil visits club. Night dangers; Tom's servants lodged.

**Ch XVIII:** Club at "Pig and Turnip": Fullbil growls; Bobbs' five-minutes theory; Fullbil: "My good friend Bobbs, I see your nose gradually is turning red." Fancher on Chinese. Dr. Chord on kites. Fullbil: Ireland "not in Italy." Tom's Galway story. Flixton arrives.

**Ch XIX:** Paddy and Jem at "Red Slipper" mug-house; Jem sings ballad; Paddy at gentlemen's table; valet's "loriot" speech.

**Ch XX:** Kensington Gardens Sunday; Chord's gossip (Marquis of Stubblington, Lord Gram, Banellic girls, Countess Cheer). Tom meets Lady Mary; her glance back; she looks back.

**Ch XXI:** Tom's father's story of Mollie (gossip, Ballygowagly girl). Chord introduces Countess and Mary; Tom watches.

**Ch XXII:** Tom tells Chord he will marry Mary; Chord worried. Chord claims he saved Countess with hot rum. Plan: scale wall.

**Ch XXIII:** Supper plan: Chord advises climbing an oak. Morning: Tom climbs oak; Chord flees; gardener Strammers points blunderbuss.

**Ch XXIV:** Strammers marches Tom through little door; Lady Mary ("French pears," "Strammers"). Mary takes blunderbuss, says "I'm afraid it's loaded." Tom declares love; interrupted; Paddy and Jem arrive.

**Ch XXV:** Paddy and Jem befriend Strammers; Strammers invites them to garden next Sunday. Tom returns to inn.

**Ch XXVI:** Saturday night: Chord visits, warns about papers; suggests giving to Paddy. Tom lets Paddy hold; Chord's inquiry suspicious.

**Ch XXVII:** Sunday: Paddy and Jem fight Westport household in garden (Countess uses ebony stick). Tom enters house, finds Lady Mary's room; locks in; papers; Mary says papers are inheritance; Tom kisses Mary. Mary tells Tom to see Mr. Josiah Brooks, Temple; Countess shouts about Chord's treachery.

**Ch XXVIII:** Tom in St. Patrick's chapel, meets Father Donovan (in London on pilgrimage to Rome, O'Gorman bequest; to sail from Rye). Chord beaten at inn by Paddy and Jem; Chord flees, swears legal action.

**Ch XXIX:** Brooks at Temple: papers examined; Brede estate in Sussex, 50–60 miles; Brooks suggests Rye as starting point. Tom refuses courts. Father Donovan goes to Rome via Rye.

**Ch XXX:** Brooks gives 500 guineas (from Mary). Nine ruffians attack Tom at inn; Tom disarms eight, one captain; swords delivered to Temple. Tailor's clothes. Paddy and Jem ride to Rye with papers (fake papers given to them instead). Tom and Father Donovan leave London next morning.

**Ch XXXI:** Ride London to Rye; Father Donovan's stories. Jem Bottles robs nine Westport men (Chord among them) on Maidstone road: piles saddles, collects 60–70 guineas; Paddy beaten and papers taken (Jem had papers? Paddy said they took them). Maidstone dinner. Rye inn.

**Ch XXXII:** Rye. Tom hires nine men led by Tom Peel (smuggler giant). Buys provisions and blunderbusses, carts of ale. Father Donovan insists on coming. Brede House taken; caretaker and family sent to village. Tunnel with secret passage; Peel's men. Sir Goddard Oxenbridge ghost. Lord Strepp approaches with troops; blunderbuss fire scatters them. Lord Strepp: "You shall pay for this." Night: Westport men attempt tunnel; Tom sends Peel; Strepp captured in tunnel, parleys ("King O'Ruddy").

**Ch XXXIII:** Paddy falls through trap-door into dungeon. Tom rides to Manor House in village with Peel's escort. Earl and Countess; Countess rages, slaps Tom. Tom scatters gold ("the dowry"). Lady Mary: "I can never marry a man I do not love." Countess forces consent; Mary asks Father Donovan's blessing. Wedding by Father Donovan in chapel. Closing: Tom writes memoirs at Lady Mary's request; children Patrick, Little Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.
